scope: Lightweight Phase 5.0 planning contract. Existing graph/engine type definitions are retained only as historical proposals and are outside the current MVP.

APPROVED_POLICY.resolver: decision-register.json#/approved_policy_baseline[].decision_id; ranges must expand to exact IDs

ARTIFACT.namespace: A00-A17 historical registry identifiers; only A01 is active in the proposed MVP

SOURCE_DOCUMENT.resolver: Git tree at source_commit; ref_id must be exact path

EVIDENCE.resolver: matching recorded command, workflow run, or hashed report

ACCEPTANCE_GATE.resolver: acceptance-gates.json or exact approved release-gate source

EXTERNAL_CONDITION.resolver: explicit condition registry in this file; never artifact ID

CONTRACT_ARTIFACT.resolver: exact path in this PR; source commit is the final PR head

external_conditions.description: Owner approval for any later Phase 5.1 scope
Owner approval of the Phase 5.0 contract
Owner decision to accept or close the Phase 5 contract gates
CI evidence for the exact final PR commit, reported externally in the PR body or final report
All approved Phase 5 output artifacts validated against the approved contract

HARD_PREREQUISITE.definition: Target decision must be resolved before source decision can be finalized
HARD_PREREQUISITE.effect: Only this type enters proposed decision-order DAG

INFLUENCES.definition: Target may inform source; no mandatory order

CO_DECISION.definition: Members are reviewed and decided as one coordinated decision package; individual decisions remain distinct
CO_DECISION.effect: Suggests joint review only; does not resolve or approve members

CONSTRAINED_BY_POLICY.definition: Decision is bounded by an already approved policy

REQUIRES_EVIDENCE.definition: Decision requires identified evidence before owner resolution

BLOCKS_EXECUTION.definition: Open decision blocks a specified future execution scope
BLOCKS_EXECUTION.effect: Blocks only specified scope; no Phase 5.0 task allocation

decision_relation_policy.legacy_dependencies_classification: INFLUENCES unless source evidence proves a hard prerequisite; all current links lack owner-approved ordering evidence and are not scheduling blockers
decision_relation_policy.co_decision_groups_require: unique group_id, at least 2 existing distinct P5 decisions; group membership does not change OPEN status

decision_review_groups.rationale: deliverable definition, allocation, canonical model and validator interfaces
capacity, effort, agent/token and cost estimates plus discovery/delivery application
value, priority and uncertainty inputs are interdependent
weekly cycle, acceptance and replan need coordinated rules

graph_node_types.definition: Outcome-sized, independently testable/releasable proposal; not a WBS node
evidence_requirements: source refs for claims; approval evidence for commitment/release
validation_rules: no operational deliverables generated in Phase 5.0
commitment requires required estimate fields and owner approval

graph_node_types.definition: Product capability reference with bounded owner
evidence_requirements: resolvable source reference
validation_rules: Phase 4 source is immutable

graph_node_types.definition: Calendar planning window no longer than seven days
evidence_requirements: measured capacity and approved schedule
validation_rules: end-start <= 6 days; multi-cycle capability uses slices or documented exception model; no actual week allocation in Phase 5.0

graph_node_types.definition: Stage or product checkpoint, distinct from release readiness
evidence_requirements: approved stage policy and observable acceptance
validation_rules: achievement requires evidence; no milestone dates invented

graph_node_types.definition: Reference to an existing approved release gate
evidence_requirements: exact policy version and execution evidence for PASS
validation_rules: no new gate or SKIPPED-to-PASS coercion

evidence_requirements: hypothesis, timebox, result and review date
validation_rules: timebox uses approved O5-09 policy; no fabricated durations

graph_node_types.definition: Evidence-backed forecast or actual measurement for one metric
evidence_requirements: source or explicit unknown rationale; measured values require measurement evidence
validation_rules: UNKNOWN and NOT_MEASURED are not numeric zero; NOT_APPLICABLE needs rationale/evidence; estimate is not measurement

graph_node_types.definition: Human role, agent, tool, infrastructure or environment capacity
evidence_requirements: owner and period-specific availability evidence
validation_rules: unknown capacity is not zero or unlimited

graph_node_types.definition: Reference to an approved policy or an open owner decision
evidence_requirements: resolve to register/source; preserve source status
validation_rules: no decision state upgrade without explicit owner evidence

graph_node_types.definition: Typed, immutable reference to an external Phase 4 work item, requirement, test or source; the referenced source is not copied or mutated
graph_node_types.id_namespace: typed external namespace; e.g. phase4-work:<id> or evidence:<sha>
evidence_requirements: exact namespace, source version and resolvable identifier
validation_rules: Phase 4 graph and mapping remain immutable
missing external ref is invalid

evidence_requirements: resolvable source and evidence
validation_rules: never infer schedule order

graph_edge_types.definition: Allocates a specific portion of a Phase 4 work node
evidence_requirements: certified snapshot ref; no ancestor/descendant double count
validation_rules: no Phase 4 graph mutation; unique allocation invariant

graph_edge_types.definition: Assigns one deliverable to one cycle; multi-week exception proposal uses weekly slices
graph_edge_types.cardinality: 0..1 week per slice; 1..N slices per capability only via approved exception model
evidence_requirements: approved estimates, measured capacity and documented exception where needed
validation_rules: weekly window <=7 calendar days; trace-only relation cannot commit work

evidence_requirements: explicit source/owner evidence
validation_rules: acyclic when approved as hard prerequisite

graph_edge_types.definition: Existing release gate required in a scoped release case
evidence_requirements: approved gate source
validation_rules: no new gate

graph_edge_types.definition: Decision blocks only the affected scoped execution
evidence_requirements: scope-specific source evidence
validation_rules: no Phase 5.0 task allocation

graph_edge_types.definition: Acceptance oracle or evidence validates deliverable
evidence_requirements: version-matched evidence
validation_rules: must resolve at commitment

graph_edge_types.definition: Associates required resource quantity and period
evidence_requirements: owner/capacity evidence for commitment
validation_rules: unknown availability cannot pass capacity check

graph_edge_types.definition: Deliverable contributes evidence toward a milestone
graph_edge_types.cardinality: 0..N contributors per milestone; 0..N milestones per deliverable
evidence_requirements: source/acceptance mapping
graph_edge_types.effect: TRACE_ONLY; milestone achievement is separately gated
validation_rules: does not equate deliverable release with stage completion

graph_edge_types.definition: Links deliverable to one typed estimate record per metric and estimate version
graph_edge_types.cardinality: 0..N; at most one active record per metric and version
evidence_requirements: source and assumptions; measured value requires measurement evidence
validation_rules: unknown states remain explicit; required estimates before commitment

graph_edge_types.definition: Discovery investigates an uncertainty attached to a deliverable
evidence_requirements: approved timebox and result evidence
validation_rules: does not itself approve an estimate or deliverable

graph_edge_types.definition: Discovery output informs an estimate record
evidence_requirements: observed discovery result
validation_rules: no automatic estimate approval

graph_edge_types.definition: Discovery result informs a decision reference
evidence_requirements: observed evidence and exact decision ref
validation_rules: does not resolve owner decision

graph_edge_types.definition: Partitions a parent capability outcome into a bounded, independently testable work slice for a documented multi-week exception
graph_edge_types.direction: parent outcome to child weekly slice
graph_edge_types.cardinality: 0..N slices per parent; each slice belongs to at most one parent
evidence_requirements: approved exception record, slice oracle and allocation reconciliation
validation_rules: each slice is <=7 days, independently testable, not product release by itself; parent roll-up is never double counted

multi_week_options.model: one deliverable references multiple weeks plus a scoped exception record
multi_week_options.example: one capability spans two weekly cycles; each cycle has a testable intermediate outcome
drawbacks: risk of treating multiple weeks as one long cycle
multi_week_options.data_effect: SCHEDULED_IN becomes 0..N under explicit exception object
multi_week_options.acceptance_effect: each week needs intermediate observable criteria and final release criteria
multi_week_options.double_count_effect: one deliverable estimate split across week allocations; totals reconcile to parent
multi_week_options.capacity_effect: requires per-cycle capacity and capped effort
multi_week_options.blueprint_alignment: requires exception evidence; weekly windows remain <=7 days
multi_week_options.recommendation: Option B is provisionally preferred because the existing conceptual model separates capability/outcome from weekly work slices

multi_week_options.model: parent capability/outcome with independently estimable seven-day work slices
multi_week_options.example: a capability spanning two cycles is represented by two weekly slices, each testable; user-visible release remains a separate final acceptance
multi_week_options.data_effect: parent Deliverable has child slices; each slice has one SCHEDULED_IN edge to one week
multi_week_options.acceptance_effect: per-slice progress evidence does not claim product release; final acceptance references release evidence separately
multi_week_options.double_count_effect: parent is a roll-up only and never counted alongside child estimate allocations
multi_week_options.capacity_effect: each slice has independent cap and owner capacity; reforecast at each boundary
multi_week_options.blueprint_alignment: weekly timebox stays <=7 days; exception requires rationale, alternatives, ceiling, interim output and review date

multi_week_options.model: separate release deliverable and implementation work packages
multi_week_options.example: one final release deliverable spans work packages each allocated to separate seven-day weeks
benefits: clear separation of release from work
drawbacks: introduces extra graph type and ownership boundaries
multi_week_options.data_effect: adds work-package entity and release relation
multi_week_options.acceptance_effect: intermediate work package acceptance differs from product release acceptance
multi_week_options.capacity_effect: work-package estimates align with team capacity windows
multi_week_options.blueprint_alignment: weekly windows remain <=7 days; exception records still required
multi_week_options.recommendation: not preferred until multiple-team consumer is demonstrated

calendar_duration.missing: UNKNOWN allowed before commitment; blocks commitment
calendar_duration.commitment_effect: Required and must be ESTIMATED or MEASURED with source before COMMITTED; UNKNOWN/NOT_MEASURED/PENDING_APPROVAL blocks commitment; NOT_APPLICABLE needs rationale and evidence.
calendar_duration.approval_requirement: Owner approval of scope and estimate basis is required before COMMITTED; measurement itself does not imply approval.

rules: development and operating cost are separate
calendar time differs from person effort
agent runtime is separate from human time
no real estimates may be fabricated in Phase 5.0
commitment exceptions require owner approval and cannot be invented
cost estimate remains required before commitment even when no cost constraint is declared
development cost, operating cost, tool cost, token usage and infrastructure are distinct metrics

multi_week_exception_record_required: documented reason the capability cannot reasonably be split into safe, independently valuable slices
split alternatives considered and why rejected
owner-approved development and operating cost ceilings, with currency and period
measurable intermediate output and test oracle per <=7-day cycle
explicitly state intermediate output is not a product release
estimate allocation reconciliation to prevent parent/child double count

multi_week_model.parent_semantics: outcome/roll-up only; not independently scheduled or double counted when slices are allocated
multi_week_model.slice_semantics: each child slice has independent acceptance oracle and at most one SCHEDULED_IN edge to a <=7-day WEEK
multi_week_model.release_semantics: intermediate work evidence cannot be treated as successful public product release

current_mvp_contract.unknown_policy: UNKNOWN is neither zero nor permission to commit
current_mvp_contract.legacy_graph_schema: Definitions below are not required for MVP implementation and confer no owner approval.
